The genuine start, and a record under another key that reuses its event_id: only the end's own key's records are candidates, so the decoy changes nothing.
The genuine start and a record of another type that the same key signed under its event_id: every candidate is graded and the worst reading stands.
The same two candidates held in the other order: the same reading.
Two candidates that fail on different checks: the worse check, the type, is reported.
The same two candidates in the other order: the same reading.
The start held twice, byte for byte: the held records are a set, so it is one candidate and nothing is ambiguous.
A tool call end whose run.started_event_id is its own event_id, read with nothing held: it names no other record, so its start is not held.
The same end, with a copy of itself in the held records: the record itself is not one of its held records, so the copy is set aside and the reading is the same.
Two different records under the end's key and event_id that both pair: the ambiguity is named.

A start and its end, beside a record of another type under the same key and the start's event_id: the end reads failed against that record, and still ends this start, because an end is graded against each start on its own. The held record at run.seq 4 shows a gap before this start.
The start carries the end's run id under another root run id: one operation is in one invocation.

A tool call end names a start in another invocation of the same conversation, both ids differing: the conversation exception is for approvals only.

The only record that names the start does not itself verify: it ends nothing.
The only record that names the start is in a version the reader does not know: it ends nothing.
A record that does not itself verify and a good end both name the start: one end.
The same two records held in the other order.
The only end is signed by another key: it ends nothing.
The only end carries another run id: it is another operation's end.
The only end names another tool: it is not this call's end.
The end's envelope key in upper case: a key compares as a key.
The start's envelope key in upper case, read from the end.
A tool call that started as read_balance and ended as transfer_funds.
The end hides the tool name, and its hash is the hash of the start's name.
The start names the tool with a lone surrogate, which JCS cannot encode: it commits to nothing, so no hidden hash matches it.
Both halves name the tool in clear with the same lone surrogate: the values are the same, so the halves agree.
The end hides a tool name whose hash is not the hash of the start's name.
A model call that started at one provider and ended at another.
A model call that started as chat and ended as embeddings.
An approval whose two halves name one action, one decider and one policy.
The answer names another action than the request: a reader would see action Y approved when X was shown.
A request to a human answered by a model.
The two halves name two policies.
Action and decider both differ: the fields are checked in a fixed order, the action first.
An end with no start, read on its own: steps 1 to 6 verify it.
The invocation's run_opened says this adapter cannot capture a tool call start: end only, start not observed.
The same end carrying the start time its source reported: shown, and still no start was signed live.
No run_opened: the declaration is on the invocation's first record.
A one-record invocation: the end is the first record and carries the declaration.
The declaration is on a run_opened another key signed.
The run_opened declares nothing: an end with no start is a finding.
The declaration names model call starts, not tool call starts.
The declaration is on another invocation's run_opened.
A cannot-capture list on a record that is not the invocation's first.
agent.run_opened is the invocation's first record, at seq 0.
The adapter replaced credential-shaped values before hashing, and says so: a reader shows it.
A file's content is its bytes, never rewritten.
A previous_hash with no context.chain_key: a link of a chain that names no chain, which no SDK builds.
A data: URI carries content, not a locator.
A protocol marker with a newline.
message_bytes_hash in upper case, as message_hash may be.
message_bytes_hash that is not a SHA-256: the schema checks its form, and nothing grades its value.
A chain key is an id, sent in private mode: free text is refused.
A tool call id is sent in private mode: free text is refused.
A response id is sent in private mode: free text is refused.
otel.scope.name is a package name: free text is refused.
otel.scope.version is a semantic version: free text is refused.
authority.scope holds at most 32 labels.
The run closed completed, and an approval request it lists has no answer it lists.
The same run closed interrupted: no finding.
The run closed completed, and every start it lists has an end it lists.
The run closed completed and lists a start whose end it does not list.
The run closed completed, and the record held under its listed end's event_id does not itself verify: the reader does not hold that end, so the closing record is not judged.
The run closed completed over a start and its end, and the reader holds only the start: the closing record is not judged, and no open operation is claimed.
A closing record of any status is judged only on every record it lists.
The listed end is held only under another key: it is not this run's record.
Neither listed record is held: step 7 reports both, in list order, and the first is the reading's reason.
Three records listed and only the middle one held: both absent records are reported, in list order.
The closing record lists its own event_id beside a start and its end, and the verifier holds the start and the end: its own id is not held, so the closing record is not judged.
The same closing record, with a copy of itself in the held records: the record itself is not one of its held records, so the copy is set aside and the reading is the same.

The closing record lists records the verifier does not hold, beside a first record in another mode: the closing record reads incomplete, and step 7 still runs every sub-step, so the mode finding of step 7f is made.
Eleven records listed, and the ones at index 2 and index 10 not held: step 7 reports /2 before /10, in list order and not in string order.
The run closed completed and lists an agent.step.occurred: it is one record and no operation, so nothing is open and there is no finding.
The adapter saw the run end interrupted and the caller said completed: the check reads the adapter's status only.
Every listed record is held under the run's key, the start ended; another key's record under the start's event_id has no end: it is not this run's.
A decision in full mode read beside its invocation's run_opened in private mode: one invocation, two modes.
The same two records, the run_opened signed by another key: an invocation is one key's, so there is no finding.
Two modes in one invocation under one key, on two chains: still one invocation.
The sender's record, beside a received record signed by the key the sender names that names a third key as its sender: not candidates for each other, so their counts are not compared.
The same two records read from the receiver: the same reading on both sides.
Two agent.handoff.sent records of one message under two keys that name each other, with different counts: a pair is one sent and one received record, so they are not compared.
The received record writes the message hash in upper case: one message, compared case-insensitively, and its counts differ.
An approval answered under another run id in the same invocation: the exception needs both ids to differ.
An approval answered in another invocation under the request's run id: the exception needs both ids to differ.
sanning.agent/1 followed by a newline: $ is the end of the string, with no exception for a final newline.
sanning.agent/ with ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT ONE: a digit is an ASCII digit.
A run id followed by a newline, which a search for ^...$ in Python would accept: refused.
A package version whose major is ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT ONE: refused.
run.seq 0 with a previous record named: not the first record, and not any other.
No previous record, at run.seq 14: not the first record, and not any other.
The invocation's run_opened declares nothing, and a later record under the same key also sits at run.seq 0 and declares: two first records are none, so the declaration does not count.
The declaring run_opened held twice, byte for byte: one record, so one first record.
A record at run.seq 0 beside the invocation's run_opened, also at run.seq 0, under the same key.
Two different records at run.seq 6 of one invocation under one key.
A decision in full mode, beside a first record in private mode and a second decision at the same position: the findings in step order, 7f, then 7g, then 7i.
A held record under the same event_id, key and position with other bytes: it is another record, so the position holds two.
The record under test is also in the held records: one record, no duplicate. No closing record is held.
Two records at run.seq 0 of one root run id under two keys: not one invocation.
Two records at run.seq 0 under one key in two invocations.
A hidden field present and a cannot-capture list off the first record: the hidden rule is read first.
A revealed field not listed and a cannot-capture list off the first record: revealed_field_unlisted is read first.
A cannot-capture list off the first record and more file parts than parts: capture_not_at_head is read first.
More file parts than parts, and a list of unchecked held parts with no count: file_parts_exceed_parts is read first.
A count that is not the list's length and more than the file parts: unchecked_held_parts_mismatch is read first.
A count that is not the list's length and an index past the parts: unchecked_held_parts_mismatch is read first.
More unchecked held parts than file parts, and an index past the parts: unchecked_held_parts_exceed_file_parts is read first.
A cannot-capture list off the first record and a record count that is not the list's length: capture_not_at_head is read first.
A cannot-capture list off the first record and a failed file with no reason: capture_not_at_head is read first.
A failed file with no reason and a hidden path present: the hidden rule is read first.
An observed start time with month 99: an RFC 3339 time has month 01 to 12.
A hand-off content type with a NUL: no control characters.
A package name with ~, which no registry admits in a new name.
A closing reason is a code from a closed list: free text is refused.
A file record in standard mode: the path, the source, the destination and the size reach Sanning only in full.
A file record in full mode: the path, the source, the destination and the size reach Sanning only in full.
A salt in upper-case hex: the salt is 32 lowercase hex characters.
A salt of 31 hex characters: 128 bits are 32.
A salt of 64 hex characters: the salt is exactly 32, never more.
A case id that fails the id grammar is refused, never left out or rewritten.
agent.step.ended with outcome.status skipped: the operation never ran because a policy, a hook or an approval stopped it.
agent.model_call.ended with outcome.status skipped: the operation never ran because a policy, a hook or an approval stopped it.
agent.tool_call.ended with outcome.status skipped: the operation never ran because a policy, a hook or an approval stopped it.
agent.retrieval.ended with outcome.status skipped: the operation never ran because a policy, a hook or an approval stopped it.
skipped ends an operation, never a run: it is not a closing status.
not_run is not a status: the word is skipped.
An approval answered with the person's text in place of the tool's result: the verdict responded.
A file record is completed or failed, never skipped: the shared outcome words do not apply to it.
A file record is completed or failed, never interrupted: the shared outcome words do not apply to it.
respond, the framework's word, is not a verdict: verdicts are past tense.
The approval of this tool call resolved rejected, and the call ended completed: it ran after its approval refused it.

The end's only candidate start is another tool call's, and an answer under this key refused the start the end names: the end reads failed at step 7a, and step 7 still runs every sub-step, so the finding of step 7h is made.
The approval resolved responded, and the call ended failed: anything but skipped is a run.
The approval resolved rejected, and the call ended interrupted: an interrupt ends the call before any answer, so no finding.
The approval resolved rejected, and the call ended skipped: no finding.
The approval resolved responded, and the call ended skipped: no finding.
The approval resolved approved, and the call ended completed: no finding.
The approval resolved edited, and the call ran with the edited action: no finding.
A rejection signed by another key names this call: it is not this agent's approval, and no finding is made.
A rejection of another action, beside this call's end: no finding.
The only rejection does not itself verify: it refuses nothing.
The rejection and a completed end, read from the call's start: the finding is on the end, not the start.
The call ended interrupted at the interrupt, and the rejection arrived in the resumed invocation: no end is written after the resume, and no finding.
The same rejection, read from the answer: it pairs with its request across the two invocations.
The call ended completed, and a rejection of its start under the same key was written in another invocation: a refusal from any invocation counts.
A policy rejected the call, a later answer approved it, and it ended completed: any refusal of the start counts, so an escalation still shows the finding.
The rejection names no request (run.started_event_id null, as after a resume with no store): it is still the agent's signed refusal, and counts.
A completed call after a rejection, its start not held, a gap before it: the findings in step order, 7a, then 7h, then 7i.
The run closed completed over a tool call its approval refused, which ended skipped: the call is ended, and no operation is open.
A decision at run.seq 14 read beside its invocation's run_opened at 0: the positions between are not held, so the run may be incomplete.
The record at run.seq 13 is held: nothing is missing directly before this one, whatever is missing further back.
Only a later record is held: a slice, not a gap.
The record at run.seq 0 is held under another key: it is not this invocation's.
The record at run.seq 0 is another invocation's.
The record at run.seq 13 is held and does not itself verify: it takes no part, so the position before this record has no record that counts.
The only earlier record does not itself verify: it takes no part, so no gap is seen.
The run_opened promises a closing record, and the verifier holds records of the invocation but no closing record: the run may be incomplete.
The run_opened read beside its invocation's closing record: no finding.
The only closing record is signed by another key: not this invocation's.
The only closing record is another invocation's.
The only closing record does not itself verify: it closes nothing.
A custom name in upper case: a-z, 0-9, underscore and dot only.
A custom name of 65 characters: at most 64.
A custom name of 64 characters, the most allowed.
A custom name with a space: free text is refused.
A custom name of a digit and two dots: no segment is empty or starts with a digit.
An empty custom name: a name has at least one segment.
A custom name that is one dot: two empty segments.
A custom name with two dots in a row: an empty segment.
A custom name that starts with a dot: an empty first segment.
A custom name that ends with a dot: an empty last segment.
A custom name whose first segment starts with a digit.
A custom name whose second segment starts with a digit: every segment starts with a letter.
A custom name whose first segment starts with an underscore.
A custom name whose second segment starts with an underscore: every segment starts with a letter.
A custom name with a hyphen: a-z, 0-9, underscore and dot only.
A custom name with a non-ASCII letter: a-z is the 26 ASCII letters.
A custom name of one letter, the shortest allowed.
A custom name of one segment: a dot is not required.
A custom name of four one-letter segments.
A custom name whose segments hold digits and underscores after the first letter, a trailing underscore included.
A dotted custom name of 64 characters, the most allowed.
A custom value revealed in clear and listed.
A custom value in clear with no context.revealed entry.
A custom name, like a decision name, cannot be hidden.
agent.run_opened with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.run_closed with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.step.started with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.step.ended with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.model_call.started with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.model_call.ended with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.tool_call.started with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.tool_call.ended with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.retrieval.started with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.retrieval.ended with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.approval.requested with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.approval.resolved with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.handoff.sent with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.handoff.received with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.decision with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.custom with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.file with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.error with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
agent.step.occurred with no context.salt: every agent record carries one.
A plain event record with a salt of 32 lowercase hex characters: outside this vocabulary, so no verdict, and the salt is in its form.
A plain event record with no salt: the salt is optional outside the agent types, so it still reads.
A runner.egress record that claims the agent vocabulary and carries a salt in upper case: step 1 reads the misplaced version first.
An event record with a salt in upper-case hex: a salt present in the wrong form reads failed on any type.
A checkpoint record with a salt of 31 hex characters: a salt present in the wrong form reads failed on any type.
A declaration record with a salt of 64 hex characters: a salt present in the wrong form reads failed on any type.
A runner.run_opened record with a salt followed by a newline: a salt present in the wrong form reads failed on any type.
A runner.run_closed record with a salt that is a number: a salt present in the wrong form reads failed on any type.
A runner.egress record with a salt written as null, which is present: a salt present in the wrong form reads failed on any type.
A runner.relay record with a salt with a character that is not hex: a salt present in the wrong form reads failed on any type.

An agent.decision with a salt in upper-case hex and an unknown member metadata.foo: the salt is read at step 4 with the rest of the schema, where unknown_field comes before bad_value. It is not read at step 1.
An agent.tool_call.started with a salt in upper-case hex and no extras.event_schema: step 2 reads the version before step 4 reads the salt.
An event record with a salt in upper-case hex and no extras member at all: step 1 reads the salt without extras.
A chained event record whose context carries chain_key before a salt in upper-case hex: step 1 reads the salt wherever it sits among the context members, and the other members are the profile's.
An agent.step.occurred that carries the outcome of an operation: a step that occurred is not an operation.
An agent.step.occurred that carries a link to a start: a step that occurred is not an operation.
An agent.step.occurred that carries a start time a source reported: a step that occurred is not an operation.
An agent.step.occurred that carries the client of a model call: a step that occurred is not an operation.
An agent.step.occurred that carries the tool and its call id: a step that occurred is not an operation.
An agent.step.occurred that carries the model a call requested: a step that occurred is not an operation.
An agent.step.occurred that carries the provider of a model call: a step that occurred is not an operation.
An agent.step.occurred that carries a model's response: a step that occurred is not an operation.
An agent.step.occurred that carries a model call's token counts: a step that occurred is not an operation.
An agent.step.occurred that carries an OpenTelemetry operation name: a step that occurred is not an operation.
An agent.step.occurred whose run.source_type is free text: it is a dotted name, as custom.name is.
An agent.step.occurred whose run.source_type is 65 characters: a dotted name is at most 64.
An agent.step.occurred whose run.source_type is 64 characters: the longest dotted name.
A retry between two attempts of a tool call, written as a step that occurred inside the call, with its name.
An agent.step.occurred whose run.source_type is "1..": no segment is empty or starts with a digit.
An agent.step.occurred whose run.source_type is "a..b": an empty segment.
An agent.step.occurred whose run.source_type is "retry.": an empty last segment.
An agent.step.occurred whose run.source_type is "retry.1x": a segment that starts with a digit.
An agent.step.occurred whose run.source_type is "agent-action": a hyphen is not allowed.
An agent.step.occurred whose run.source_type is "AgentAction": upper case is not allowed.
An agent.step.occurred whose run.source_type is one segment: a dot is not required.
An agent.step.occurred with run.name hidden: absent in clear, its hash listed in context.hidden.
An agent.step.occurred outside any operation: its run_id is the root_run_id and its parent_run_id is null.
A record whose run.parent_run_id is the run_id of a held agent.step.occurred: the parent is not an operation, so there is nothing to look for and no finding.
An agent.step.occurred read beside the step it occurs inside: it is one record, so it has no start to find and no end to wait for.
A step end names an agent.step.occurred as its start: a step that occurred begins nothing.
